newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says foils assassination attempts.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says foils assassination attempts.

text.p: A Sudanese minister said in comments published on Monday that police had arrested a group of Communist party members who were planning to assassinate political figures and carry out other acts of violence.
The official news agency SUNA quoted Culture & Information Minister Brigadier Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair as saying neighbouring Eritrea was behind the alleged plotters.

"The security authorities have detected a network administered by remnants of the dissolved Communist party who were supported by foreign circles and who wanted to carry out subversive acts against public establishments and political assassinations," Khair said.

"The act comes within the context of a series of plots being woven by the Eritrean regime of (President) Isayas Afeworki who is utilising his cadres who are specialised in criminal and subersive acts," he added.

He said Afeworki was exploiting "elements in the alliance of agents and traitors". Northern and southern rebels opposed to the Khartoum government have formed an umbrella group called the National Democratic Alliance with the aim of toppling the Sudanese government.
Khair did not say how many people had been arrested and did not give any further details.
Sudan has accused Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of helping the rebels but all three countries deny the charge.
